primitives.name: Game Pace Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: We analysed game-related statistics for each quarter of the eight games played by the USA using a k-means cluster analysis to classify game pace using ball possessions per game quarter.
primitives.latex: \text{Ball Possessions} = \text{Field Goals Attempted} + \text{Offensive Rebounds} + \text{Turnovers} - 0.4 \times \text{Free Throws Attempted}
primitives.assumptions: Game pace is quantifiable via ball possession counts; clusters represent distinct temporal dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ball possession rates fall below threshold, cluster assignment becomes ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic model of game-state evolution based on possession-based clustering.
layer2.telemetry: Cluster centroids derived from k-means algorithm applied to ball possession data.

primitives.name: Point Differential Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: How differences in game-related statistics affected point differentials was examined using linear regression.
primitives.assumptions: Linear relationship exists between recovered balls and field goals with point differentials; residuals are normally distributed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When game context shifts beyond linear model applicability, predictive accuracy degrades.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's state transition function where recovered balls and field goals act as input variables affecting score progression.
layer2.telemetry: Coefficients from linear regression fit to observed game statistics.

primitives.name: Recovery Efficiency Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: The largest structure coefficient between game paces for the USA was for recovered balls (0.33, P 5 0.001).
primitives.assumptions: Recovery events directly correlate with offensive opportunities; normalized by ball possession count.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In low possession games, REI may overestimate impact due to denominator instability.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to compute real-time tactical adjustments based on opponent turnover recovery.

reasoning_traces.think:
Game pace classification uses k-means clustering on ball possession counts per quarter to distinguish fast vs. slow games. Ball possession is defined as field goals attempted plus offensive rebounds minus turnovers plus 0.4 times free throws attempted. This metric allows for temporal segmentation of game intensity. Point differential modeling applies linear regression to quantify how game statistics like recovered balls and field goals influence scoring outcomes. Structure coefficients indicate that recovered balls have a strong correlation with game pace (0.33), suggesting that high-intensity play correlates with increased ball recovery. Recovery efficiency index normalizes these events against ball possession, offering a scalable measure of defensive assertiveness. These primitives form a dual framework: one for categorizing game tempo and another for predicting outcome variability through statistical modeling.
